name: Allow s3:GetObject on * fenced by a Deny with NotResource to one approved WHOLE BUCKET (no broad exfil, but the surviving whole-bucket read is account-undetermined)
note: A data-perimeter guardrail: read is allowed broadly, but an explicit Deny with NotResource excludes everything except the approved bucket, confining the effective read to that one bucket. The broad-exfil (DATA-EXFIL) capability is correctly removed - but the SURVIVING spared scope is still a WHOLE-bucket read on a canonical S3 bucket ARN whose owning account cannot be resolved, so it must NOT read CLEAN (S1-R1-deny-fence-surviving).
rationale: NotResource in a Deny statement applies the Deny to every resource EXCEPT those listed. Here s3:GetObject is denied on all resources except arn:aws:s3:::approved-data/*, so the broad Allow is fenced down to a single bucket. Because explicit Deny wins and the Deny covers everything outside approved-data/*, there is no BROAD object-read (DATA-EXFIL) capability - so DATA-EXFIL must NOT fire, and flagging broad exfil here would overstate the risk. But the read the fence leaves standing is still a WHOLE-bucket read (approved-data/*) on a canonical S3 bucket ARN that carries no account field and is not pinned by an aws:ResourceAccount / s3:ResourceAccount condition; its owning account cannot be resolved from the policy text, so the tool CANNOT clear it as a same-account read. The archetypal exfil primitive must never silently clear (threat-model: S3 bucket ARNs are account-blind; a fenced-down remnant of a broad exfil grant does not become safe). It surfaces at INFO as CROSS-ACCOUNT-DATA-READ-UNDETERMINED, an UNPROVEN (not confirmed) crossing (threat-model T8: no overstated certainty). Ref: AWS docs, 'IAM JSON policy elements: NotResource' + explicit-Deny precedence.
